definitions.explanation: The total amount of money collected by a government through taxation. Commonly used in news and policy discussions.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{税収|ぜいしゅう}は{過去最高|かこさいこう}だった。
examples.english: This year's tax revenue was the highest ever.

examples.japanese: {景気|けいき}が{悪化|あっか}すると{税収|ぜいしゅう}が{減|へ}る。
examples.english: When the economy worsens, tax revenue decreases.

examples.japanese: {税収|ぜいしゅう}の{不足|ふそく}を{補|おぎな}うために{国債|こくさい}を{発行|はっこう}する{方針|ほうしん}が{示|しめ}された。
examples.english: A policy was announced to issue government bonds to make up for the shortfall in tax revenue.

notes:
A compound of {税|ぜい} (tax) and {収|しゅう} (income, revenue). An abbreviation of {税金|ぜいきん}{収入|しゅうにゅう}.

Frequently appears in news reporting about government budgets and fiscal policy.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {税収|ぜいしゅう}が{増|ふ}える (tax revenue increases)
- {税収|ぜいしゅう}が{落|お}ち{込|こ}む (tax revenue drops)
- {税収|ぜいしゅう}{不足|ふそく} (tax revenue shortfall)
- {過去最高|かこさいこう}の{税収|ぜいしゅう} (record-high tax revenue)
- {国|くに}の{税収|ぜいしゅう} (national tax revenue)
